subject: Request: Detailed exportability & retention checklist for audit trails
messages:
From: Sam Johnson <sam.johnson@stratafin.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@stratafin.com
Date: Tue, 14 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Audit trail exportability — checklist & clarifications

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As part of our RFP scoring we need a compact, question-by-question confirmation on your audit logging and export capabilities. Can you confirm the following items for our security and legal teams? A short yes/no plus a 1-2 line explanation for each would be ideal.

1) Export formats supported (NDJSON, Parquet, CSV, gzipped bundles) and whether exports preserve original event ordering.
2) Ability to slice exports by customer-id, time range, and request-id, including maximum parallel export jobs.
3) Hashing/tamper evidence: are exported bundles accompanied by checksums and a signed manifest; do you support immutable snapshots?
4) Chain-of-custody / provenance metadata included (ingest timestamps, source partition, host id, sequence numbers).
5) Encryption and key management for at-rest exports (KMS/HSM integration; customer-managed keys).
6) Support for legal hold (pause deletion) and ability to produce a preservation package on demand.
7) Typical delivery SLA for a 1TB export to our S3 (role-based s3:// path) and options for accelerated delivery.
8) Mechanism to attest to export completeness (sampling index, row counts, delta checks).
9) Redaction capabilities — what fields can be redacted on export and redaction logs retained?
10) Any constraints for on-prem/private deployments vs hosted (network, tooling, access to raw storage).

We'd like the checklist by end of day Thursday (2026-12-16). If there are sample manifests or a short playbook you can attach that would be very helpful for our legal review.

Best,
Sam
Sam Johnson
Senior Information Security Manager
StrataFin Capital
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Sam Johnson <sam.johnson@stratafin.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Dec 2026 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Audit trail exportability — checklist & clarifications

Sam — thanks for the clear list. We're on it. I've looped in Marissa (account lead) and Ben (security PM) to assemble the formal checklist and attach our playbook. Attached: redwood_audit_export_playbook.pdf (high-level runbook) and rfi_response_sheet.xlsx (answer-by-question).

Quick notes while we prepare the document:
- We'll confirm supported export formats (NDJSON and Parquet are standard; CSV available for small slices). Exports preserve event ordering per-partition; full-global ordering depends on ingestion topology — we'll call out specifics.
- Slicing: customer-id/time-range/request-id supported; we can run up to N concurrent export workers per-account in hosted; Dedicated/Private deployments can scale further.
- Tamper evidence: we attach SHA256 checksums and a signed manifest; for forensic requests we offer an immutable snapshot option (write-once object store or signed ledger entry).
- KMS: hosted supports customer-managed keys (CMK) via partner KMS; private deployments can use on-prem HSMs.
- Legal hold: supported — preserves objects and prevents GC; preservation packages produced within committed SLA.

We'll provide the formal per-question answers in the attached sheet and follow up with a sample manifest. If StrataFin has a preferred manifest schema, please share (you mentioned one in the RFP).

Irene
Irene Choi
Director, Security Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- redwood_audit_export_playbook.pdf (summary of export steps, packaging, and verification)
- rfi_response_sheet.xlsx (Q/A matrix)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Sam Johnson <sam.johnson@stratafin.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Dec 2026 10:24:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Audit trail exportability — checklist & clarifications

Sam — thanks, adding the concrete answers below (pulled from the draft sheet). Irene / Ben: please confirm or edit before Thursday.

1) Formats: NDJSON (line-delimited JSON) and Parquet (columnar) supported officially; CSV export supported for slices < 2GB. All exports are delivered compressed (gz by default). Exports preserve ordering per ingestion partition (yes) — global sequence can be reconstructed using sequence numbers in the manifest.

2) Slicing & parallelism: slice by customer_id, time range, request_id, and event_type. Hosted export service supports up to 8 parallel workers per account by default; we can request elastic slots for larger jobs (Dedicated can go higher).

3) Tamper evidence: yes. Every bundle includes SHA256 checksums for each file and a signed manifest (RSA-2048 signature). For customers requiring cryptographic immutability we provide an option to timestamp and anchor the manifest entries to a third-party ledger.

4) Provenance metadata: manifests include ingest_timestamp_utc, source_node_id, partition_id, offset, and sequence_number. We also include original request headers when available.

5) Encryption/KMS: exports are encrypted at rest with AES-256. Hosted customers can opt into using their CMK via our KMS integration (AWS KMS / Azure Key Vault). Private deployments can integrate with on-prem HSMs.

6) Legal hold: supported; legal-hold flags prevent object deletion and can be scoped to account/namespace. Preservation packages include both raw bundles and a human-readable index.

7) Delivery SLA: typical bulk export (<=1TB) to a customer S3 endpoint: 48–72 hours for standard pipeline; accelerated expedited delivery (24–36 hours) available at premium. Smaller slices (<100GB) commonly complete within 8–12 hours.

8) Attestation to completeness: manifests include total row_count and a sampling index (hash-prefix samples) plus a delta-check summary for incremental exports. We also provide an integrity_report.json summarizing checksums and counts.

9) Redaction: we support field-level redaction rules at export time (PII tokenization or redaction); redaction operations themselves are logged in a redaction_audit.log bundled with the export. Note: redaction may affect cryptographic equivalence checks — the manifest will note redaction markers.

10) Hosted vs Private constraints: hosted: no direct raw storage access; exports are delivered by our export service to customer S3; Private/on-prem: direct access to raw object storage and local export tooling, network egress policies depend on customer environment. We'll call out networking/port requirements in the playbook.

Next steps: Irene / Ben, can you confirm the RSA signature strength (we default to RSA-2048 but support RSA-4096 on request) and whether StrataFin requires ledger anchoring? Sam — I've also attached an example integrity_report and a short sample manifest for your review.

Thanks,
Marissa
VP, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced:
- sample_manifest_v1.json (example of manifest layout)
- integrity_report_sample.json

Marissa / Irene — this is great, thanks for the rapid turnaround. A few follow-ups from legal/security: 

• Please attach the sample_manifest_v1.json and the integrity_report_sample.json directly into the RFP bundle (we want to include them in the submission to our GC).
• For the delivery SLA: can you confirm cost/lead time tradeoffs for expedited delivery (we may require 24-hour for critical subpoenas)?
• Please provide a redwood-generated sample of the redaction_audit.log for a redaction job (anonymized).
• Can you confirm whether the RSA-4096 option is available for signing manifests and whether ledger anchoring is an add-on (and if so, estimated cost model)?

Also attaching our expected_manifest_schema (StrataFin_expected_manifest_v1.json) for compatibility checks. If you can return a one-paragraph compatibility statement against that schema we can mark the item as satisfied.

If possible we'd like the final Q/A workbook and the three samples (manifest, integrity report, redaction_audit) by EOD Friday 2026-12-17.

Regards,
Sam
